analysis:
The change is confined to scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py, an offline unittest that asserts the shape of .github/workflows/ci.yml. The updated assertions (head lines ~232-266, 347-351, 704-708) expect macOS provider, summary, SDK and cluster-metadata jobs to take `runs-on` from `fromJSON(needs.route.outputs.routes)[lane]`. They also expect the jobs to depend on `route` and the route job to request one `macos_arm64` lane per provider shard, with the Blacksmith runner as the fallback. Nothing in this file changes provider runtime behavior, keys, attestation, the coordinator WebSocket contract, or the prefix cache (T-041), so no product threat IDs are directly affected.

The CI-integrity angle is that the tests still assert `continue-on-error` is absent, `fail-fast: false` on the shards, and the required-gate structure, so test strength is retained. Two points are outside the supplied evidence and I did not verify them. First, the actual ci.yml change is in another file and was not supplied. Second, the Darkbloom macOS sandbox runner trust and isolation are unknown: untrusted PR code may run on a routed runner, and whether secrets or caches are exposed to it cannot be determined here. The test retains SAVE_CACHES gating (pull requests never save caches) and `persist-credentials: false`, which limits the exposure. The reviewer of ci.yml should check that the route output cannot be influenced by PR-controlled input and that the routed runners are isolated. I found no concrete regression in this file.
